questions.question: As notified in April 2025, a research study of which of the following institutes revealed that surface ozone is silently threatening India’s food crops?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Indian Institute of Technology, Kharagpur**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A significant research study conducted by the **Indian Institute of Technology (IIT), Kharagpur**, notified in **April 2025**, has highlighted the grave impact of **surface ozone** on India's agricultural productivity.
 
• The study revealed that **surface ozone**, also known as **tropospheric ozone**, is acting as a "silent threat," significantly reducing the yields of essential **food crops** such as **wheat**, **rice**, and **maize**. ***Hence, the statement regarding IIT Kharagpur is correct.***
 
• Researchers at **IIT Kharagpur** utilized advanced **satellite data** and **ground-based observations** to monitor the concentration of ozone across the **Indo-Gangetic Plain (IGP)** and other major agricultural hubs.
 
• The findings indicate that high levels of **surface ozone** lead to **oxidative stress** in plants, which damages their **photosynthetic** capabilities and results in stunted growth and lower grain quality.
 
• The study warns that if emissions of **precursor gases** like **nitrogen oxides (NOx)** and **volatile organic compounds (VOCs)** are not controlled, the loss in crop production could pose a serious risk to **India’s food security** by **2030**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Surface Ozone (Tropospheric Ozone):**

 
 
• Unlike the **stratospheric ozone** layer that protects Earth from **ultraviolet (UV) radiation**, **surface ozone** is a harmful **secondary pollutant**.
 
• It is formed when **pollutants** emitted by **cars**, **power plants**, and **industrial boilers** react chemically in the presence of **sunlight**.
 
• It is a major component of **smog** and is highly **reactive**, affecting both human health and **vegetation**.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Plant Physiology:**
 
 
• Ozone enters the plant through the **stomata** (pores on the leaf surface) during gas exchange.
 
• Once inside, it triggers the production of **reactive oxygen species (ROS)**, which damage **chlorophyll** and reduce the **biomass** of the plant.
 
• In **India**, the **Indo-Gangetic Plain** is most vulnerable due to the high density of **anthropogenic emissions** and favorable **meteorological conditions** for ozone formation.
 
 
 
• **Economic and Nutritional Consequences:**
 
 
• Reduced crop yields lead to higher **food prices** and economic losses for **farmers**.
 
• Research suggests that **ozone pollution** can decrease the **protein content** and essential minerals in **cereal crops**, affecting the nutritional intake of the population.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Precursor Gases:** The primary chemicals responsible for ozone formation are **Nitrogen Oxides (NOx)** and **Volatile Organic Compounds (VOCs)**. These are largely produced by **vehicle exhausts** and **biomass burning**.
 
• **Monitoring Agencies:** In **India**, agencies like the **Central Pollution Control Board (CPCB)** and the **System of Air Quality and Weather Forecasting And Research (SAFAR)** are responsible for monitoring **air quality indices**, including ozone levels.
 
• **Global Context:** Similar studies in **China** and the **United States** have also shown that ozone can reduce crop productivity by **5% to 20%**, making it a **global environmental challenge** for the **21st century**.

questions.question: Which authority of India hosted the 25th Meeting of the South Asian Telecommunication Regulators’ Council (SATRC‑25)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Telecom Regulatory Authority of India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Telecom Regulatory Authority of India** (**TRAI**) hosted the **25th Meeting of the South Asian Telecommunication Regulators’ Council** (**SATRC-25**).
 
• The event was held in **New Delhi**, **India**, from **November 11 to 13, 2024**.
 
• This landmark meeting marked the **Silver Jubilee** of the council, celebrating **25 years** of regulatory cooperation in the **South Asian** region.
 
• The meeting was organized by the **Asia-Pacific Telecommunity** (**APT**) and hosted by **TRAI** to foster collaboration in the **telecommunication** and **Information and Communication Technology** (**ICT**) sectors.
 
• The session was inaugurated by the **Minister of State for Communications** and **Rural Development**, **Shri Pemmasani Chandra Sekhar**, alongside **Anil Kumar Lahoti**, the **Chairman** of **TRAI**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **South Asian Telecommunication Regulators’ Council (SATRC):**

 
 
• **SATRC** was formed in **1997** under the umbrella of the **Asia-Pacific Telecommunity** (**APT**).
 
• It consists of **9 member countries**: **Afghanistan**, **Bangladesh**, **Bhutan**, **India**, **Iran**, **Maldives**, **Nepal**, **Pakistan**, and **Sri Lanka**.
 
• The council serves as a forum for regulators to exchange views and harmonize policies on **spectrum management**, **licensing**, and **digital transformation**.
 
 
 
• **Telecom Regulatory Authority of India (TRAI):**
 
 
• **TRAI** is a statutory body established on **February 20, 1997**, by the **Telecom Regulatory Authority of India Act, 1997**.
 
• Its primary **function** is to regulate **telecommunication services**, including fixation/revision of tariffs, to ensure a fair and transparent environment in the **Indian** telecom market.
 
• It is headquartered in **New Delhi**.
 
 
 
• **Asia-Pacific Telecommunity (APT):**
 
 
• Established in **1979**, the **APT** is an intergovernmental organization focused on the development of **ICT** in the **Asia-Pacific** region.
 
• It plays a crucial role in coordinating regional positions for global forums like the **International Telecommunication Union** (**ITU**).
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **SATRC Action Plan Phase IX:** The **25th meeting** focused on the implementation of the **Action Plan Phase IX**, which covers the period of **2024-2025**.
 
• **Key Themes:** The discussions at **SATRC-25** revolved around the deployment of **5G technology**, enhancing **cybersecurity**, and utilizing **satellite communication** to bridge the **digital divide**.
 
• **Regulators' Roundtable:** A major highlight was the **Regulators' Roundtable**, where heads of regulatory bodies discussed **emerging technologies** and **regulatory sandboxes** to promote innovation.
 
• **Digital India Initiative:** The hosting of this event by **India** aligns with the broader goals of the **Digital India** program, showcasing **India’s** leadership in **affordable data** and **digital public infrastructure** (**DPI**).

questions.question: In June 2025, Bhashini signed an MoU with which government entity to integrate real‑time translation on passenger platforms?

options.text: Ministry of Communications and Information Technology

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Centre for Railway Information Systems**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **June 2025**, **Bhashini** (Digital India Bhashini Division) entered into a strategic Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the **Centre for Railway Information Systems (CRIS)**.
 
• The partnership is designed to integrate **AI-led real-time translation** capabilities into various **passenger platforms** and digital services of the **Indian Railways**.
 
• The primary goal of this collaboration is to break **language barriers** for commuters, allowing them to access **railway announcements**, **ticketing information**, and **emergency instructions** in their **native languages**.
 
• **CRIS**, acting as the technical arm of the **Ministry of Railways**, will deploy these **Natural Language Processing (NLP)** tools across **mobile applications** and **automated public address systems** at stations.
 
• This initiative is a significant step under the **Bhashini Mission** to empower citizens by providing **voice-based and text-based** digital services in **22 scheduled Indian languages**.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Centre for Railway Information Systems.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bhashini Mission:**

 
 
• Launched by the **Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY)**, Bhashini is India's **Artificial Intelligence**-led language translation platform.
 
• It aims to enable easy access to the internet and digital services in **Indian languages**, fostering a more inclusive **digital ecosystem**.
 
• The mission utilizes **crowdsourcing** through the **Bhasha Daan** initiative to collect diverse language datasets for training **AI models**.
 
 
 
• **Centre for Railway Information Systems (CRIS):**
 
 
• Established in **1986**, CRIS is an autonomous organization under the **Ministry of Railways** located in **New Delhi**.
 
• It is responsible for developing and managing major **IT systems** for the railways, including the **Passenger Reservation System (PRS)** and the **Unreserved Ticketing System (UTS)**.
 
• By partnering with Bhashini, CRIS aims to enhance **passenger experience** for domestic tourists and **migrant workers** who may not be proficient in English or Hindi.
 
 
 
• **Real-time Translation Features:**
 
 
• The technology involves **Speech-to-Speech** and **Speech-to-Text** translation, specifically optimized for the **noisy environments** of **railway platforms**.
 
• It helps in providing **real-time updates** on **train schedules**, **platform changes**, and **safety protocols** in regional dialects.
 
• The integration supports the **Digital India** vision of making government services accessible to everyone regardless of their linguistic background.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Technological Impact:** This MoU signifies the use of **Deep Learning** and **Machine Learning** to solve practical **governance and service delivery** challenges in a linguistically diverse country like **India**.
 
• **Scalability:** The success of this integration on **passenger platforms** is expected to lead to similar implementations in other public sectors like **banking**, **healthcare**, and **education**.
 
• **Date of Event:** The collaboration was formalized in **June 2025**, marking a milestone in the **AI adoption roadmap** of the **Government of India**.

questions.question: Which of the following countries became the member of National Development Bank in May 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Algeria**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Algeria** has officially been granted membership to the **New Development Bank (NDB)**, also known as the **BRICS Bank**, as confirmed by the bank’s President **Dilma Rousseff**.
 
• The announcement regarding **Algeria**'s admission was made during the **9th Annual Meeting** of the Board of Governors of the **NDB** held in **Cape Town**, **South Africa**.
 
• Membership in the **New Development Bank** allows **Algeria** to access a new source of funding for its **infrastructure** and **economic development** projects, reducing its reliance on traditional Western financial institutions.
 
• The move is part of **Algeria**'s broader strategic goal to integrate with the **BRICS** economic bloc and diversify its international partnerships. ***Hence, the correct answer is Algeria.***
 
• The **NDB** membership is open to any member of the **United Nations**, and **Algeria** joins other recent members such as **Egypt**, **Bangladesh**, and the **United Arab Emirates** in expanding the bank's global footprint.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **New Development Bank (NDB):**

 
 
• The **NDB** was established in **July 2014** during the **6th BRICS Summit** held in **Fortaleza**, **Brazil**.
 
• It formally commenced its operations in **2015** with its headquarters located in **Shanghai**, **China**.
 
• The founding members include **Brazil**, **Russia**, **India**, **China**, and **South Africa**.
 
• The primary mandate of the bank is to mobilize resources for **infrastructure** and **sustainable development** projects in **emerging markets** and **developing countries**.
 
 
 
• **Membership Expansion Strategy:**
 
 
• In **September 2021**, the **NDB** admitted the **United Arab Emirates**, **Uruguay**, and **Bangladesh** as its first expansion members.
 
• **Egypt** completed its accession process and officially became a member in **February 2023**.
 
• The bank aims to provide a platform for cooperation among **developing nations** and serves as an alternative to the **World Bank** and the **International Monetary Fund (IMF)**.
 
 
 
• **About Algeria:**
 
 
• **Algeria** is the largest country in **Africa** by land area and is a major exporter of **petroleum** and **natural gas**.
 
• The country’s entry into the **NDB** signifies a shift in its economic policy toward **multipolar** financial cooperation.
 
• **Algeria** applied for membership to the **NDB** with a reported contribution of **1.5 billion dollars** to the bank's capital.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Financial Structure:** The **NDB** has an initial authorized capital of **100 billion US dollars** and an initial subscribed capital of **50 billion US dollars**.
 
• **Leadership:** The first President of the **NDB** was **K. V. Kamath** from **India**. The current President is **Dilma Rousseff**, the former President of **Brazil**, who assumed office in **2023**.
 
• **Governance:** Unlike the **World Bank**, where voting power is based on shareholding, the **NDB** founding members initially held **equal voting rights**, and no founding member has **veto power**.

questions.question: What is the new Loan-to-Value (LTV) ratio, set by the Reserve Bank of India for loans below ₹2.5 lakh in June 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**85%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**, in its regulatory update for **June 2025**, has revised the **Loan-to-Value (LTV) ratio** to **85%** for loans amounting to less than **₹2.5 lakh**.
 
• The primary objective of this adjustment is to facilitate easier **credit flow** to small-scale borrowers and individuals in the **unorganized sector** who require small-ticket funding for personal or business needs.
 
• By setting the **LTV at 85%**, the **RBI** has effectively reduced the margin requirement for borrowers to **15%**, allowing them to leverage a higher percentage of their collateral's value.
 
• This specific ratio applies to a variety of small-ticket credit products, including **gold loans** and micro-business loans, helping to drive **financial inclusion** across the country.
 
• The move is designed to mitigate the credit gap and provide a safety net for **micro-borrowers**, ensuring that they are not forced toward informal, high-interest money lenders.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Loan-to-Value (LTV) Ratio**:

 
 
• The **LTV ratio** is a critical financial metric used by lenders to assess the lending risk before approving a loan. It is calculated by dividing the loan amount by the **appraised value** of the asset being used as collateral.
 
• A higher **LTV ratio** (such as **85%**) means the borrower provides a smaller down payment, while a lower LTV provides a higher "equity cushion" for the bank.
 
 
 
• **Role of the Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**:
 
 
• Established on **April 1, 1935**, the **RBI** is India's central bank. It regulates the **monetary policy** and supervises the banking sector to maintain **financial stability**.
 
• The **RBI** uses regulatory tools like **LTV caps** to prevent over-leveraging in specific sectors like **housing**, **automobiles**, or **gold**, thereby protecting the health of the **banking system**.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Financial Inclusion**:
 
 
• By increasing the **LTV to 85%** for loans below **₹2.5 lakh**, the government and the **central bank** aim to empower the **Priority Sector**.
 
• This change particularly benefits **Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs)** and low-income households, allowing them to access capital with minimal upfront equity.
 
 
 
• **Regulatory Guidelines and Risk Management**:
 
 
• While the **LTV** is increased to provide relief, the **RBI** mandates that banks and **Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs)** conduct rigorous **credit appraisals** and maintain **Capital Adequacy Ratios (CAR)**.
 
• The policy ensures that while credit is accessible, it does not lead to a rise in **Non-Performing Assets (NPAs)** within the financial ecosystem.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Threshold Limit**: The **85% LTV** specifically targets the "bottom of the pyramid" by capping the loan amount at **₹2.5 lakh**. Loans exceeding this amount are subject to different, often stricter, LTV guidelines.
 
• **Collateral Valuation**: Under **RBI guidelines**, lenders must follow a transparent process for valuing the collateral (like **gold jewellery** or **property**) to ensure the **85%** limit is applied accurately and ethically.
 
• **Implementation Date**: The new norms were highlighted as a key shift in the **RBI's June 2025** monetary policy review, reflecting the evolving economic landscape and the need for **liquidity support** in the micro-loan segment.

questions.question: As reported in July 2025, what is the name of the new ultra-rare blood antigen discovered in a woman from the Kolar district of Karnataka?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**CRIB**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **July 2025**, medical researchers identified a new ultra-rare blood antigen named **CRIB**.
 
• The discovery was made in a woman residing in the **Kolar district** of **Karnataka**, India.
 
• The identification of the **CRIB** antigen occurred during routine blood screening or cross-matching, where the patient's blood showed an unusual reaction that did not match existing known **blood group systems**.
 
• This finding is classified as **ultra-rare**, meaning it is found in an extremely small percentage of the global population, often making it difficult to find compatible **blood donors** for transfusions.
 
• The discovery highlights the genetic diversity within the Indian population and the importance of advanced **immunohematology** labs in detecting such rare phenotypes to ensure patient safety during medical procedures.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Blood Antigens**: These are **proteins** or **sugars** located on the surface of **red blood cells**. They determine a person's blood type and trigger an immune response if incompatible blood is introduced into the body.
 
• **Rare Blood Groups in India**:
 
 
• **Bombay Blood Group (hh)**: First discovered in **1952** in **Mumbai** by **Dr. Y.M. Bhende**. It is found in roughly **1 in 10,000** individuals in India.
 
• **EMM Negative**: A rare blood group recently identified in **Gujarat** in **2022**. People with this type lack the **EMM antigen** on their red blood cells.
 
 
 
• **Rh-null (Golden Blood)**: This is considered the rarest blood type in the world, lacking all **61 antigens** in the **Rh system**. Since its discovery, fewer than **50 cases** have been reported globally.
 
• **International Society of Blood Transfusion (ISBT)**: This organization is responsible for the official classification of **blood group systems**. As of **2023-2024**, there are **45 recognized systems**, including **ABO**, **Rh**, **Kell**, and **Duffy**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Transfusion Challenges**: Individuals with ultra-rare antigens like **CRIB** cannot receive blood from common donors (O, A, B, AB). They require blood from donors who also possess (or lack) the same specific antigen to avoid **hemolytic transfusion reactions**.
 
• **Genetic Mapping**: Regions like **Karnataka** and other parts of Southern India have shown unique **allelic frequencies** due to historical endogamy, leading to the discovery of several rare blood phenotypes.
 
• **Registry**: The **Indian Society of Blood Transfusion and Immunohaematology (ISBTI)** and various regional registries work to maintain databases of rare donors to assist in emergencies involving rare types like **CRIB**.

questions.question: Which of the following banks launched a TAB-based digital onboarding process for Non-Resident Indians (NRIs) in January 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**State Bank of India**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **State Bank of India (SBI)**, India's largest public sector lender, officially launched its **TAB-based digital onboarding process** for **Non-Resident Indians (NRIs)** in **January 2025**.
 
• This initiative is designed to simplify and expedite the account opening journey for the **Indian Diaspora**, allowing bank officials to onboard customers digitally using **tablets** during outreach programs or at branch locations.
 
• The process eliminates the need for physical forms and extensive paperwork, significantly reducing the **turnaround time (TAT)** for activating **NRI accounts**.
 
• The launch is part of **SBI's** broader **digital transformation** strategy aimed at leveraging technology to enhance the banking experience for its global customer base of over **480 million** users.
 
• By implementing this **TAB-based solution**, the bank aims to capture a larger share of the **remittance market** and strengthen its relationship with the **32 million** strong Indian community residing abroad.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **NRI Banking Products**:

 
 
• **NRE (Non-Resident External) Account**: Allows NRIs to park their foreign earnings in **Indian Rupees**; both principal and interest are fully **repatriable**.
 
• **NRO (Non-Resident Ordinary) Account**: Used to manage income earned within India, such as **rent, dividends, or pension**; it is subject to Indian **tax laws**.
 
• **FCNR (Foreign Currency Non-Resident)**: Fixed deposit accounts maintained in **foreign currencies** (like USD, GBP, Euro) to avoid exchange rate fluctuations.
 
 
 
• **State Bank of India Global Reach**:
 
 
• As of **2025**, SBI maintains a massive international presence with over **230 offices** across **29 countries**, including major hubs like the **USA, UK, Singapore, and UAE**.
 
• The bank's digital flagship, **YONO (You Only Need One)**, has also been expanded as **YONO Global** to provide specialized services to customers in various international jurisdictions.
 
 
 
• **Technological Advancements**:
 
 
• Apart from the TAB-based onboarding, the bank has invested heavily in **Artificial Intelligence (AI)** and **Machine Learning (ML)** to provide personalized wealth management services to high-net-worth **NRI customers**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Regulatory Compliance**: The digital onboarding process adheres strictly to the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** guidelines regarding **Know Your Customer (KYC)** and **Anti-Money Laundering (AML)** standards to ensure secure transactions.
 
• **Document Requirements**: Under the digital process, NRIs are still required to provide scanned copies of a **valid Indian Passport** or **OCI (Overseas Citizen of India) card**, **valid Visa/Work Permit**, and **foreign residence proof**.
 
• **FEMA Regulations**: All NRI banking activities are governed by the **Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA), 1999**, which regulates the flow of foreign exchange and the maintenance of accounts by persons resident outside India.
 
• **Market Position**: **State Bank of India** accounts for nearly **one-fourth** of the total market share in the Indian banking sector and is a **Systemically Important Bank (D-SIB)** in the domestic economy.

questions.question: Who became the first Indian chess player to rank World No. 1 in live chess ratings in 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**R Praggnanandhaa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **January 2025**, **Rameshbabu Praggnanandhaa** achieved a historic milestone by becoming the first Indian chess player to reach the **World No. 1** position in the **live chess ratings** since the era of **Viswanathan Anand**.
 
• He secured this top spot during his performance at the **Tata Steel Chess Tournament** held in **Wijk aan Zee**, **Netherlands**.
 
• By gaining significant rating points through consistent victories, he managed to surpass the live rating of the legendary Norwegian Grandmaster **Magnus Carlsen**, who had dominated the top position for over a decade.
 
• At the age of **19**, **Praggnanandhaa** has become one of the youngest players in history to occupy the **World No. 1** rank in the real-time rating system.
 
• This achievement highlights the "golden age" of **Indian chess**, where multiple young grandmasters from the country are competing at the highest levels of the sport globally.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rameshbabu Praggnanandhaa**:

 
 
• Born in **August 2005** in **Chennai**, **Tamil Nadu**, he is a child prodigy who earned the **Grandmaster** title in **2018** at the age of **12 years, 10 months, and 13 days**.
 
• He gained worldwide fame for defeating **Magnus Carlsen** in several rapid and online games before making his mark in the classical format.
 
• His sister, **R Vaishali**, is also a **Grandmaster**, making them the first-ever brother-sister duo to hold the **Grandmaster** title.
 
 
 
• **Live Chess Ratings vs. FIDE Ratings**:
 
 
• **Live ratings** are calculated and updated instantly after every rated game played in international tournaments.
 
• In contrast, the **FIDE** (International Chess Federation) publishes the **official rating list** only once a month, typically on the **1st** of every **month**.
 
• Reaching **World No. 1** in live ratings is a prestigious indicator of a player's current peak performance and form.
 
 
 
• **The Indian Chess Renaissance**:
 
 
• **Viswanathan Anand** was the first Indian to become a **Grandmaster** in **1988** and later became a **five-time World Champion**.
 
• Other prominent Indian players include **D Gukesh**, who won the **Candidates Tournament 2024** to become the youngest world championship challenger, and **Arjun Erigaisi**, who breached the **2800 Elo** rating mark in **2024**.
 
• India's dominance was solidified at the **45th FIDE Chess Olympiad** in **Budapest** in **2024**, where both the **men's** and **women's** teams won historic **Gold Medals**.
 
 
 
• **Elo Rating System**:
 
 
• The **Elo rating system** is the method used to calculate the relative skill levels of players in zero-sum games like chess.
 
• A rating above **2800** is considered "Super Grandmaster" territory and is usually achieved only by a handful of players in the world at any given time.

questions.question: Which round of talks between India and the European Union for a Free Trade Agreement kicked off on 12 May 2025, in Brussels?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**11th**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **11th round** of negotiations between **India** and the **European Union (EU)** for a comprehensive **Free Trade Agreement (FTA)** commenced on **12 May 2025**.
 
• This high-level meeting took place in **Brussels**, **Belgium**, which serves as the administrative heart of the **European Union**.
 
• The talks represent a continued effort to bridge gaps in areas such as **market access**, **digital trade**, and **sustainable development**. ***Hence, the statement regarding the 11th round is correct.***
 
• The primary objective of these negotiations is to create a balanced and ambitious trade deal that benefits both economies by reducing **customs duties** and enhancing the **ease of doing business**.
 
• Delegations from both sides worked on finalizing various chapters of the agreement, including **rules of origin** and **technical barriers to trade (TBT)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Historical Context:**

 
 
• The **India-EU** trade negotiations were first launched in **2007** but were suspended in **2013** due to significant differences over **market access** and **labor standards**.
 
• Negotiations were formally **relaunched** on **17 June 2022** during a meeting in **Brussels**, aiming for a deeper strategic partnership.
 
 
 
• **Triple Track Approach:**
 
 
• The current engagement is not limited to trade alone; it follows a triple track involving a **Free Trade Agreement (FTA)**, an **Investment Protection Agreement (IPA)**, and an agreement on **Geographical Indications (GIs)**.
 
 
 
• **Bilateral Trade Statistics:**
 
 
• The **European Union** is **India's second-largest trading partner** after the **USA**, accounting for a significant portion of India's total global trade.
 
• Major Indian exports to the **EU** include **textiles**, **chemicals**, **pharmaceuticals**, and **engineering goods**.
 
 
 
• **Key EU Member States:**
 
 
• The **EU** consists of **27 member countries**, including major economies like **Germany**, **France**, and **Italy**, all of which have a vested interest in the Indian market.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **CBAM Concerns:** A major talking point in recent rounds, including the **11th round**, has been the **Carbon Border Adjustment Mechanism (CBAM)** introduced by the **EU**, which could impact Indian exports of **steel**, **aluminum**, and **cement**.
 
• **Services Sector:** India is pushing for greater mobility for its **professionals** (Mode 4 of trade in services) and recognition of its **data-secure status** to boost the **IT and enabled services** sector.
 
• **Investment Protection:** The **IPA** aims to provide a stable legal framework for investors from both regions, ensuring protection against **discriminatory treatment** and **expropriation**.
 
• **Geographical Indications:** The **GI Agreement** is designed to protect traditional products like **Darjeeling Tea** from India and **Champagne** or **Feta Cheese** from the **EU**, ensuring they are not imitated in each other's markets.

questions.question: Who is the youngest female para swimmer in the world to cross the English Channel and a recipient of the World Open Water Swimming Association (WOWSA) Award, 2024, for Adaptive Performance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Jiya Rai**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jiya Rai**, a **16-year-old** para-swimmer from **India**, achieved the monumental feat of becoming the **youngest** and **fastest** female para-swimmer in the world to swim across the **English Channel** in **July 2024**.
 
• She completed the grueling swim from **Abbot’s Cliff** in the **United Kingdom** to **Pointe de la Courte-Dune** in **France**, covering a distance of **34 kilometers** in a remarkable time of **17 hours and 25 minutes**.
 
• In recognition of her extraordinary determination and skill, she was conferred with the **World Open Water Swimming Association (WOWSA) Award, 2024**, in the **Adaptive Performance of the Year** category.
 
• **Jiya Rai** was diagnosed with **Autism Spectrum Disorder** at a young age, and she has utilized swimming not only as a therapy but also as a platform to showcase elite athletic capability on a global stage.
 
• Before her **English Channel** success, she gained international fame in **March 2022** by swimming across the **Palk Strait** from **Talaimannar** (Sri Lanka) to **Arichalmunai** (India) in **13 hours and 10 minutes**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Deepa Malik**:

 
 
• She is a legendary figure in Indian para-sports and was the **first Indian woman** to win a medal at the **Paralympic Games**, securing a **Silver medal** in **Shot Put** at the **Rio 2016 Paralympics**.
 
• She has been honored with the **Padma Shri** and the **Khel Ratna Award** for her immense contribution to sports and serves as a major inspiration for female athletes in **India**.
 
 
 
• **Prachi Yadav**:
 
 
• She is a premier Indian **Para-Canoeist** who represented the country at the **Tokyo 2020 Paralympics**.
 
• She made history by winning a **Gold medal** at the **2022 Asian Para Games** in **Hangzhou** in the **KL2** canoe event, becoming the first Indian to do so in this discipline.
 
 
 
• **Devanshi Satija**:
 
 
• She is a talented Indian **Para-swimmer** who has consistently performed at the **National Para Swimming Championships** and represented **India** at the **Asian Para Games**.
 
• She has won multiple medals in the **S10 category**, contributing to the growing prominence of para-swimming in the Indian sporting landscape.
 
 
 
• **English Channel**:
 
 
• Often referred to as the **"Everest of Swimming,"** it is a body of water separating **Southern England** from **Northern France**.
 
• The shortest distance across the channel is approximately **33.3 kilometers** (20.7 miles), but swimmers often cover much longer distances due to strong **tidal currents** and **low water temperatures** ranging from **14 to 18 degrees Celsius**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **WOWSA Awards**: These awards celebrate the world's most adventurous and courageous **open water swimmers**. The **Adaptive Performance** category specifically honors athletes with disabilities who overcome physical or neurological challenges to achieve world-class results.
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Rashtriya Bal Puraskar**: For her previous record-breaking feats, **Jiya Rai** was awarded this prestigious honor, which is the highest civilian award in **India** for individuals under the age of **18**.
 
• **Naval Background**: **Jiya Rai** is the daughter of a **Master Chief Petty Officer** in the **Indian Navy**, and her training has often been supported by the **Indian Navy's** sports facilities.

questions.question: Which of the following states/Union Territories has the largest number of wildlife sanctuaries as of 2023?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Andaman & Nicobar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Union Territory of **Andaman & Nicobar Islands** holds the distinction of having the largest number of wildlife sanctuaries in India, with a total of **96** sanctuaries as of **2023**.
 
• According to the **National Wildlife Database**, India has a total of **567 wildlife sanctuaries**, covering approximately **3.73%** of the country's total geographical area.
 
• The **Andaman & Nicobar Islands** account for a significant portion of these protected areas, despite having a relatively small landmass compared to large mainland states. ***Hence, the correct answer is Andaman & Nicobar.***
 
• These sanctuaries are vital for protecting the unique **marine life**, **tropical evergreen forests**, and **endemic species** like the **Andaman Wild Pig** and the **Narcondam Hornbill**.
 
• The **Wildlife Institute of India (WII)** and the **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)** are responsible for maintaining the records and overseeing the management of these protected areas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Wildlife Sanctuary (WLS):**

 
 
• A **Wildlife Sanctuary** is an area declared by the **State Government** or the **Central Government** under the **Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972** for the purpose of protecting, propagating, or developing wildlife or its environment.
 
• In a sanctuary, certain human activities such as **grazing**, **collection of minor forest produce**, and **private ownership rights** may be allowed as long as they do not interfere with the well-being of the animals.
 
 
 
• **State-wise Distribution:**
 
 
• **Maharashtra** follows Andaman & Nicobar with the second-highest number, hosting approximately **50** wildlife sanctuaries.
 
• **Uttar Pradesh** has **25** wildlife sanctuaries, including the famous **Hastinapur Wildlife Sanctuary**.
 
• **Kerala** manages **17** wildlife sanctuaries, such as the **Periyar Wildlife Sanctuary** and **Wayanad Wildlife Sanctuary**.
 
• **West Bengal** contains **16** wildlife sanctuaries, including the **Sajnekhali Wildlife Sanctuary** situated within the **Sundarbans**.
 
 
 
• **Geographical Facts:**
 
 
• The total area covered by wildlife sanctuaries in India is about **122,564.53 square kilometers**.
 
• The **Rann of Kutch Wildlife Sanctuary** in **Gujarat** is one of the largest sanctuaries in terms of area, spanning over **7,500 square kilometers**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972:** This **Act** provides the legal framework for the protection of various species of wild animals and plants, the management of their habitats, and the regulation and control of trade in wild animals.
 
• **Difference between National Parks and Sanctuaries:** **National Parks** enjoy a higher degree of protection where no human activity or private rights are allowed, whereas **Wildlife Sanctuaries** permit limited human interference.
 
• **Conservation Status:** As of **December 2023**, India has **106 National Parks** and **567 Wildlife Sanctuaries**, contributing to the **Integrated Development of Wildlife Habitats** scheme.
 
• **Endemic Species:** The high number of sanctuaries in **Andaman & Nicobar** is primarily due to the need to protect species that are not found anywhere else in the world (**endemic**), preserving the ecological balance of the **Bay of Bengal** region.

questions.question: In January 2025, President Droupadi Murmu, at Rashtrapati Bhavan, honoured which specific para-athlete with the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Praveen Kumar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• President **Droupadi Murmu** conferred the prestigious **Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award** for the **year 2024** upon para-athlete **Praveen Kumar** during a ceremony held at **Rashtrapati Bhavan** in **January 2025**.
 
• **Praveen Kumar** is a distinguished **Para-High Jumper** who made the **country** proud by winning the **Gold Medal** in the **Men’s High Jump T64** event at the **Paris Paralympics 2024**.
 
• During the **Paris 2024** Games, he cleared a height of **2.08 meters**, which not only secured him the top spot on the podium but also set a new **Asian Record**.
 
• This award recognizes his consistent excellence and his status as the **youngest Indian para-athlete** to win a **Gold Medal** at the **Paralympic Games** at the **age** of **21**.
 
• The **Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award** is the highest sporting honour of **India**, awarded annually by the **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Praveen Kumar.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award:**

 
 
• It was instituted in the **year 1991-92** and was formerly known as the **Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award**.
 
• The award comprises a **medallion**, a **certificate**, and a **cash prize** of **Rs. 25 lakh**.
 
• The first recipient of this award was **Chess Grandmaster Viswanathan Anand**.
 
 
 
• **Achievements of other Para-Athletes in Paris 2024:**
 
 
• **Preeti Pal:** She became the first Indian woman track and field athlete to win two medals at the **Paralympics**, securing **Bronze** in both the **100m** and **200m T35** events. She was honored with the **Arjuna Award** in the same **January 2025** ceremony.
 
• **Nishad Kumar:** A prolific **Para-High Jumper** who won a **Silver Medal** in the **T47** category at the **Paris Paralympics 2024**, repeating his performance from the **Tokyo 2020** Games.
 
• **Hokato Hotozhe Sema:** The **shot putter** from **Nagaland** was also among the athletes recognized for his **Bronze Medal** achievement in **Paris**.
 
 
 
• **National Sports Awards 2024:**
 
 
• The awards are usually announced to celebrate **National Sports Day** on **August 29**, but the ceremony for the **2024** cycle was held in **January 2025**.
 
• Apart from the **Khel Ratna**, the **Arjuna Award** was conferred upon **29 athletes**, including stars like **Neeraj Chopra** (who has previously won the Khel Ratna) and various rising para-stars.
 
• The **Dronacharya Award** was given to outstanding **coaches**, and the **Dhyan Chand Award** was given for **lifetime achievement** in sports development.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Praveen Kumar's** journey began in **Govindgarh**, **Noida**, **Uttar Pradesh**. Despite having a congenital impairment that affects one of his legs, he competed in high jump events against able-bodied athletes before transitioning to **para-sports**.
 
• The **T64 classification** in which he competes is specifically for athletes with **movement moderately affected** in one lower leg or the absence of one or both legs below the knee.
 
• His **Gold Medal** was **India's** **6th gold** at the **Paris Paralympics 2024**, contributing to the **country's** record-breaking haul of **29 medals** (7 Gold, 9 Silver, and 13 Bronze).
 
• The selection committee for the **National Sports Awards** is usually headed by a retired **Supreme Court** or **High Court Judge** and includes eminent sportspersons and sports administrators.

questions.question: How many tribal grassroots functionaries and village-level change leaders does the Aadi KARMAYOGI initiative aim to build for responsive governance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**20 lakh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Aadi KARMAYOGI** initiative is a collaborative program launched by the **Ministry of Tribal Affairs (MoTA)** in partnership with the **National Capacity Building Commission (CBC)**.
 
• The primary objective of this initiative is to build the capacity of approximately **20 lakh** (2 million) tribal grassroots functionaries and village-level change leaders across the country. ***Hence, the correct answer is 20 lakh.***
 
• It aims to foster **responsive governance** by empowering those at the bottom of the administrative pyramid to ensure the effective delivery of government schemes in tribal areas.
 
• The program focuses on enhancing the "human element" of governance, ensuring that officials and leaders are sensitized to the unique cultural and socio-economic needs of **Scheduled Tribes (STs)**.
 
• It is designed to bridge the gap between policy formulation and its execution at the **village level**, promoting a more citizen-centric approach in tribal administration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mission Karmayogi**:

 
 
• The **Aadi KARMAYOGI** program is a specialized vertical under the broader **Mission Karmayogi** (National Programme for Civil Services Capacity Building - NPCSCB).
 
• Launched on **September 2, 2020**, Mission Karmayogi aims to overhaul the Indian bureaucracy by shifting from "rules-based" to "roles-based" training.
 
• It utilizes the **iGOT-Karmayogi** (Integrated Government Online Training) platform to provide continuous learning opportunities to over **46 lakh** central employees.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Tribal Affairs (MoTA)**:
 
 
• Established in the year **1999** after the bifurcation of the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment.
 
• It is the nodal ministry for the overall policy, planning, and coordination of programs for the development of **Scheduled Tribes**.
 
• The ministry handles matters related to **Forest Rights Act (2006)** and the **PESA Act (1996)** to empower tribal self-governance.
 
 
 
• **Capacity Building Commission (CBC)**:
 
 
• Established as an independent body to assist the Prime Minister's Public Human Resources Council.
 
• It sets the standards for training institutions and monitors the implementation of **Annual Capacity Building Plans** across various ministries.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Implementation Strategy**: The initiative utilizes **State Tribal Research Institutes (TRIs)** and **National Tribal Research Institute (NTRI)** located in **New Delhi** as hubs for developing curriculum and conducting training.
 
• **Last-Mile Delivery**: By training **20 lakh** functionaries, the government intends to reach the most remote tribal habitations, ensuring that benefits of the **Tribal Sub-Plan** and other central/state grants reach the intended beneficiaries.
 
• **Digital Integration**: The training modules are often integrated with **digital tools** to track progress and ensure that the change leaders are equipped with modern administrative skills.
 
• **Socio-Economic Impact**: Strengthening grassroots leadership is expected to improve health, education, and livelihood indicators in **tribal-dominated districts** (often referred to as Aspirational Districts).

questions.question: In which event did Bindyarani Devi set a new national record at the Dehradun National Games, 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Snatch (women’s 55 kg)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bindyarani Devi**, the ace weightlifter from **Manipur**, delivered an exceptional performance at the **National Games 2025** held in **Dehradun**, **Uttarakhand**.
 
• She competed in the **women’s 55 kg** weightlifting category and established a new **national record** in the **Snatch** event.
 
• The **Snatch** is one of the two primary disciplines in weightlifting where the athlete lifts the barbell from the ground to overhead in one continuous motion.
 
• Setting a **national record** in this event highlights her technical proficiency and explosive strength, further solidifying her position as one of India's top athletes in the **55 kg** division. ***Hence, Option 4 is the correct event.***
 
• While she also competed for the **Clean and jerk** and **Total lift**, the specific milestone of a **national record** in the **2025** edition was achieved in the **Snatch** segment.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sorokhaibam Bindyarani Devi:**

 
 
• She is a prominent weightlifter hailing from the state of **Manipur**, which is often referred to as the powerhouse of Indian sports.
 
• She gained international fame by winning the **Silver Medal** in the **women's 55 kg** category at the **2022 Commonwealth Games** in **Birmingham**.
 
• Her career also includes a **Gold Medal** at the **2019 Commonwealth Weightlifting Championships** and various podium finishes at the **Asian Championships**.
 
 
 
• **National Games 2025:**
 
 
• The **38th edition** of the **National Games** was hosted by **Uttarakhand** in **2025**.
 
• The games were spread across various cities, including **Dehradun**, **Haldwani**, and **Rishikesh**, aimed at promoting sports culture in the Himalayan state.
 
• The **National Games** serve as the premier domestic multi-sport event in **India**, organized by the **Indian Olympic Association (IOA)**.
 
 
 
• **Weightlifting Technicalities:**
 
 
• **Snatch:** The first lift of the competition, requiring the bar to be moved from the floor to an arm's length overhead in a single movement.
 
• **Clean and Jerk:** A two-stage lift where the bar is first brought to the shoulders (**Clean**) and then pushed overhead (**Jerk**).
 
• **Total Lift:** The combined weight of the best successful **Snatch** and the best successful **Clean and Jerk**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Governing Body:** The **Indian Weightlifting Federation (IWLF)** is the national body responsible for the sport of weightlifting in **India**, headquartered in **New Delhi**.
 
• **Support Systems:** Top athletes like **Bindyarani Devi** receive support through the **Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS)**, an initiative by the **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports** to assist potential Olympic medal winners.
 
• **Regional Dominance:** Northeast Indian states, particularly **Manipur** and **Mizoram**, have consistently produced world-class weightlifters, including legendary figures like **Mirabai Chanu** and **Kunjarani Devi**.
 
• **Records and Standards:** National records are meticulously tracked by the **IWLF** and are categorized based on body weight classes redefined by the **International Weightlifting Federation (IWF)** in **2018**.
